title: Cost Harmonization Initiative: tactical playbook for batching, cache, and quant profiles
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: A cross-functional playbook and initiative to harmonize cost controls across batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles. Goal is to create standardized experiments, rollout gates, and runbook to deliver predictable unit-cost savings without producing detectable degredation in user-facing quality or latency SLOs.
background: We have many fragmented cost experiments (prefetch, microbatching, int8 trials) across product teams. This leads to inconsistent metrics, duplicate infra work, and risk of regressions. PMs, Eng, and DX need an operationalized framework to run safe, repeatable rollouts and to measure end-to-end economics (tokens saved vs. error/latency impact).
objectives: Unify experiment taxonomy for batching, cache, and quantization
Deliver a reusable rollout playbook (canary -> gated A/B -> fleet) with automated checks
Reduce per-token serving cost by 12% (net) across target workloads within 12 weeks
Ensure quality regressions are detected within 5k requests using eval prompt suite
key_results: KR1: Standardized experiment spec template accepted by Eng and Design
KR2: Field trial harness that runs 3 workloads in parallel and reports cost/latency/quality within 24h
KR3: Automated rollback threshold and policy implemented in console for two model families
KR4: 12% median unit cost reduction on testbed workloads with <1% output-quality delta
milestones: M1 (Week 1-2): Finalize taxonomy and experiment spec; align owners
M2 (Week 3-5): Implement field harness + dashboards; lightweight infra contracts
M3 (Week 6-8): Run controlled trials on 3 canonical workloads; collect telemetry
M4 (Week 9-10): Evaluate results, define rollout gates and rollback policies
M5 (Week 11-12): Canary rollout for Dedicated & Hosted; postmortem and playbook handoff
tasks: Build telemetry dashboard: cost-per-token, tail-latency, quality delta (owner: Observability Eng)
Integrate prefix/KV cache TTL controls into the Console model config (owner: Runtime Eng)
Create quantization profile validator that flags inputs with high semantic risk (owner: Research)
Design canary experiment in console with auto-fallback on failures (owner: Platform)
Author runbook and postmortem checklist (owner: PM)
Coordinate beta customers for Dedicated trials (owner: Solutions)
Set up eval prompt library and acceptance thresholds (owner: DX/Research)
progress_updates: 2026-01-22 — Kickoff: Align core team; agreed experiment spec skeleton. Action: PM to circulate spec draft (Aisha).

2026-02-18 — Research delivered initial quant profiles (int8 / int4 experimental). Early notes: int4 shows 18% CPU savings but higher hallucination risk on long prompts. Trial plan updated to include conservative QA sampling (Marta Ruiz).

2026-02-28 — Field harness v0 deployed in staging; first microbatching trial ran against 'summarization' workload with 7% cost improvement and 40ms median latency increase. Decided to test adaptive batch cap to control tail latency (Decision by Jonah Park).
2026-03-08 — Design review: console UX for batch/cache controls reviewed and approved with minor accessibility updates. PR: github.com/redwood/pr/4821 (linked in artifacts).
2026-03-12 — Canary gating policy drafted: automatic rollback if quality delta > 0.8% OR p99 latency regresses by >25% for 1 hour. Stakeholder review scheduled 2026-03-15.
decisions: Use a 3-stage rollout (staging -> canary 5% -> gated A/B) instead of immediate fleet toggle to limit blast radius.
Adopt conservative default quant profiles and require explicit opt-in for aggressive quantization via 'quant-profile' flag in model config.
Standardize on a single experiment metadata format (YAML) that includes workload tags, acceptance thresholds, and telemetry mapping.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions due to quantization. Mitigation: Maintain eval prompt sets per workload and run semantic-diff checks before canary promotion.
Risk: Tail latency increases from batching on small interactive requests. Mitigation: Implement adaptive batch caps and per-route latency SLOs; default batching disabled for routes with <50ms p95.
Risk: Conflicting experiments from different teams. Mitigation: Central experiment registry and weekly experiment sync; deny overlapping experiments on same routes during active trials.
